Retrieval: Full WebFetch, 18 Jul 2026. Publication 17 Jul 2026, 7:57 AM EDT.

Andy Burnham officially declared Labour Party leader Friday 17 July 2026. Takes office as Prime Minister on Monday after Starmer's resignation. (CBS states Monday; other approved sources say Monday 20 July — CBS incorrectly wrote "July 21".)

Secured nominations from 379 of 403 Labour MPs in the House of Commons. Will be the UK's seventh leader/PM since 2016. Only contender in the leadership contest to replace Starmer, who was forced out by a Labour rebellion after poor May local election results.

Direct quotes (Andy Burnham, in first speech as leader):
- "We're going to give them hope back. This is a proud moment you have given me and my family today, and an emotional one, but it is one for which I am ready."
- Pledged a politics "based on unity and hope" and an economy spreading growth across the country.
- On Trump: "The path we're on, if we are not careful, is a path towards the politics of the United States of America."

Policy priorities: economic renewal and modern industrial job creation; greater public control of key sectors; fixing social care access for ageing/disabled populations; reversing effects of 1980s privatisation.
